scope.question: Define a portable, versioned factory-as-code language and deterministic runtime that can coordinate bounded probabilistic workers across durable human interaction, parallel work, side effects, and governed evolution.
in_scope: static factory definitions and their lifecycle
typed phases, task DAGs and transitions
budgets, leases, checkpoints, retries, escalation and cancellation
gates, compensation, cleanup, reconciliation and audit
boundaries: Git is desired configuration and review history, not the authoritative live execution database.
The runtime owns instance state; an LLM/foreman may propose a route but cannot commit a transition or grant itself authority.
This is a superset/interchange model, not a claim that one vendor already implements it.
MCP/A2A/OpenAPI describe tool/peer interfaces, not workflow correctness, durable execution or authorization by themselves [S24][S25].
No unattended product authority, ambiguity resolution, privilege growth, grader/policy mutation, high-risk promotion, novel incident command, or irreversible operation is included.
scope.as_of_note: Evidence and mutable product behavior assessed to 2026-09-13.

verified_capabilities.claim: Warp Factories has an official repository-backed v1alpha1 definition. It covers factory metadata, repository scope, agent roles/prompts, execution defaults, integrations/secrets/MCP servers, runners, event/schedule automations, benchmark tasks, LLM scorers, webhooks and skills. GitHub-backed changes receive an atomic config check/apply, and live work items/runs/metrics remain outside definition files [S01][S02].
verified_capabilities.status: verified from live documentation and the unauthenticated generated JSON Schema endpoint

verified_capabilities.claim: Warp is Early Access. Its foreman chooses/skips default triage/planning/build/review stages through instructions; spec approval, questions and merge are human touchpoints by default. Review verdicts are advisory [S03].
verified_capabilities.status: officially documented availability and behavior, not independent production reliability

verified_capabilities.claim: Warp Self-improvement samples LLM-scorer failures and can open application or definition PRs after 25 unreviewed failures or seven days (or ad hoc); nothing is adopted without review [S04][S05].
verified_capabilities.status: official capability; no public denominator-based safety/effect estimate

verified_capabilities.claim: Durable engines demonstrate event history/replay, signals/updates, declarative retry, task queues and bounded histories; Kubernetes demonstrates desired/actual reconciliation [S08][S09][S10][S11][S19].
verified_capabilities.status: mature generic control-plane mechanisms, not proof of agent correctness

verified_capabilities.claim: AWS ASL and Argo show typed states, catch/retry, DAG dependencies, dynamic loops and exit handlers; GitHub Actions shows reusable pinned workflow calls and matrices [S12][S13][S14][S15][S16][S17].
verified_capabilities.status: verified workflow primitives with platform-specific semantics

verified_capabilities.claim: LangGraph provides checkpoints/threads and durable interrupts. OpenAI Agents provides handoffs and guardrails. These are useful worker/scaffold features but do not replace an external authorization and lifecycle ledger [S20][S21][S22][S23].
CloudEvents, JSON Schema 2020-12, OpenAPI 3.1.1, W3C Trace Context and SLSA provide useful event, schema/interface, correlation and provenance building blocks [S06][S07][S18][S26][S27].
verified_capabilities.status: open specifications; composition semantics must be added by this DSL

evidence_basis: Direct Warp documentation plus its generated v1alpha1 JSON Schemas were inspected, including top-level property sets. The schema exposes no declarative phase graph, transitions, typed artifacts, budgets, joins, gates, retry/compensation/cleanup, or composition [S01][S02].
Cross-checks use versioned/open workflow specifications and official runtime/framework docs, plus independent agent-system and security research [S06-S30].

Prior repository-agent-OS validated results and the self-managing-project synthesis were used to preserve fenced leases, outbox/reconciliation, exact-hash approvals, risk tiers and protected improvement controls.
limits: Warp documentation is an Early Access product contract and can change. There is no public source code for its hosted orchestrator and no independent audit of its lifecycle semantics or Self-improvement outcome rate.

Temporal, Argo, Step Functions and GitHub Actions prove orchestration primitives, not that one syntax is portable or that LLM work is correct. Runtime semantic differences include replay requirements, retry defaults, history limits, cancellation and exactly-once wording [S08-S17].
LLM scorers are stochastic and correlated with candidates. A single judge label or aggregate score is not a safety oracle [S05][S28].

MAST reports 14 failure modes from 1,600+ traces across seven multi-agent frameworks; AgentDojo shows material prompt-injection/utility tradeoffs. More agents and tool access increase failure surface [S29][S30].
Vendor feature availability is not evidence of productivity or unattended end-to-end safety. No reviewed evidence validates an autonomous plan-to-production-to-self-modification loop.
evidence_and_limits.design_consequence: Compile declarative intent into one deterministic, separately privileged control plane. Treat all agent decisions and external callbacks as untrusted proposals/events. Require local outcome data before expanding authority.

principals.authority: approve schema/policy, allowed capabilities, risk taxonomy and factory versions; cannot retroactively alter audit
supply intent and approve exact spec/decision revision; cannot approve security exceptions unless separately qualified
sole writer of canonical execution state; evaluates deterministic guards, issues leases, records events and invokes adapters; does not author candidate work
propose phase/role/decomposition/clarification; no state-write, credential minting, gate approval or budget expansion
act only through a short-lived capability lease scoped to attempt/repo/path/tool/network/budget
produce exact-artifact verification; separate identity/environment/input from author where risk requires
approve exact spec/artifact/policy digests for a named action, scope and expiry; cannot be candidate or author
enforce verbs/resources/egress and mint audience-bound credentials outside the model
dispatch eligible work, compare desired/observed state, revoke stale leases and perform allowlisted cleanup; no semantic approval
own protected eval inclusion, hidden tests, graders, thresholds and promotion; candidates have read-only or opaque access
read immutable evidence; incident commander may invoke bounded break-glass with independent confirmation and expiry

invariants: Requester, candidate/author, verifier, approver and promotion authority are distinct logical roles; high risk maps them to distinct principals.
Risk may rise automatically but may not fall because an agent reports confidence.
Definition inheritance can reduce authority but cannot add authority above tenant/repository policy.
A role name is not authorization. Every action needs authenticated principal + capability lease + policy decision + idempotency key.
All untrusted repository/web/issue/tool/MCP content remains data, never authority [S24][S25][S30].

definition_states.INVALID: validation failed; last ACTIVE stays live
definition_states.APPROVED: approval bound to manifest digest but not active
definition_states.DEPRECATED: existing instances may finish; new admission forbidden
definition_states.ROLLBACK_PENDING: prior known-good digest selected and approved
definition_states.ROLLED_BACK: prior version restored; failed version retained

instance_states.DISPATCHING: outbox intent written, worker not confirmed
instance_states.RUNNING: valid fenced lease and active phase
instance_states.PAUSED: durably resumable; no active write lease
instance_states.COMPENSATING: reverse completed side effects where declared
instance_states.RECONCILING: external outcome unknown or drift detected
instance_states.PARTIAL: explicitly accepted subset; never silently success
instance_states.DEAD_LETTER: malformed/poison event retained for operator action
instance_states.STALE: lease/factory/spec/policy version invalid; worker output rejected

complete_state_catalog.terminal_rule: Terminal is a composite invariant, not only a label: no live lease/token, all mandatory children terminal, effects reconciled, required artifacts retained, and cleanup either succeeded or has an approved bounded exception. FAILED/CANCELLED/TIMED_OUT do not bypass cleanup.
complete_state_catalog.source_basis: The catalog extends durable history/replay, typed error and exit-handler patterns rather than copying a vendor state list [S08][S12][S15].

rules: Only the controller commits transitions with compare-and-swap on aggregate revision. Duplicate event_id or idempotency_key returns the prior result.
A transaction appends event + new state + budget reservation + outbox intents atomically. External effects occur later and record receipts.
An LLM output must validate against a declared proposal schema; it emits route.proposed/question.proposed/artifact.proposed, never state.changed.
Before retry of any non-read effect, query/reconcile remote state by receipt/idempotency key. UNKNOWN_EFFECT goes to RECONCILING or human review; never blind replay.
Lease fence = monotonically increasing epoch. Heartbeat renews expiry only for the current epoch; late/stale outputs are quarantined, not attached.
Any change to spec, artifact head, factory, policy, required evidence, approver eligibility or risk invalidates dependent approvals/gates and propagates staleness downstream.
Cancellation is a durable event and scope tree. Stop new dispatch, signal children, wait grace, fence/kill, compensate in reverse dependency order, then clean.
Timers are durable absolute deadlines. Backoff is capped exponential with jitter and consumes retry/wall/cost budgets.
Reconciliation periodically derives desired versus observed state, records drift, and uses monotonic corrective actions [S19].

failure_classes.HUMAN_TIMEOUT: default declared deny/defer/cancel, never implicit approve

transition_contract.compatibility: Events are immutable. Readers ignore only declared optional fields. Breaking event/state semantic changes require a new major schema/API version plus upcaster or drain-and-migrate plan. Replay must pin workflow implementation or use explicit deterministic version markers [S08].

required_types: WorkRequest, SourceSnapshot, SpecRevision, DecisionRecord, QuestionRecord, PlanDAG
TelemetryCase, Postmortem, EvalCase, DatasetManifest, CandidateChange, PromotionDecision
contracts: Every phase declares input/output type+version, cardinality, max size/classification, producer role, validators and whether absence is legal.
Mutable collaborative objects use immutable revisions plus a stable logical ID. References bind digest/revision, never “latest.”
Large bodies live in an ACL-controlled object/artifact store. Workflow history stores digest, schema and URI only to remain bounded [S11].
An artifact becomes gate-eligible only after upload complete, digest verified, malware/secret/data-class checks pass and producer lease is current.
Derived artifacts retain all input edges. Redaction produces a new artifact with policy and reviewer provenance; it does not overwrite the original.
SLSA/in-toto-style provenance can establish origin and process, not semantic correctness [S27].
Retention and deletion are stateful auditable workflows, including tombstones and legal holds.
artifact_contracts.exact_hash_binding: Approval and verification key = tenant + work item + spec revision digest + candidate artifact/SHA + factory digest + policy digest + gate manifest digest + action scope + expiry.

durable_model.conversation: stable thread_id + participants/ACL + purpose + factory/spec version; transcript chunks are artifacts, not state
durable_model.turn: turn_id, actor principal, occurred_at, raw/normalized content digests, attachments/tool evidence, correlation/causation, classification
durable_model.question: question_id, exact question/schema/options, why needed, blocking states, requested decision owner/role, default-on-timeout, deadline, supersedes
durable_model.answer: answer_id, question_id, respondent identity/role, typed value, rationale, evidence refs, timestamp/signature
durable_model.decision: decision_id, subject, selected option, alternatives, rationale, assumptions, scope/non-goals, spec/factory/policy digests, effective/expiry, approvers, supersedes/invalidates
durable_model.handoff: from/to role, objective, authority/capability lease, exact input artifact list/digests, open questions, completed/next actions, budget remaining, acceptance contract
durable_model.summary: generated view with coverage map back to source turn IDs; never authority

protocol: Persist the user message before any action. Acknowledge with thread/decision IDs.
Validate answer against the question schema and identity/role. Conflicting answers open a conflict gate; latest prose does not silently win.
Accept a decision only after showing the normalized consequence when material. Commit it as an immutable revision. Edits/supersession create events and invalidate dependent spec/gates/work.

On context compaction, create a signed/hashed summary plus unresolved questions, accepted decisions, artifact index and last event cursor. Resume by verifying digests and replaying canonical decisions, not by trusting summary prose.
Agent handoff is accepted only if the receiver validates schemas, digests, authority and freshness; otherwise HANDOFF_REJECTED returns exact defects.
Human pause has durable timeout, reminders/escalation and an explicit fail-closed outcome. No response is never approval.
Concurrent conversation branches create decision candidates. A deterministic merge requires nonoverlapping subjects or a human conflict decision.
conversation_and_handoffs.interaction_boundary: Back-and-forth can be fully durable and resumable, but it cannot autonomously decide ambiguous product value, consent, legal/privacy interpretation or irreversible tradeoffs. The system may ask, research, offer alternatives and recommend; an accountable authorized person commits those decisions.

orchestration_and_composition.node_model: Each compiled node declares stable ID, kind={task,subfactory,switch,wait,event,human,gate,fanout,join,compensate,cleanup,end}, typed I/O, guard, dependencies, role, capability profile, queue, lease/heartbeat/timeouts, retry policy, budgets, checkpoint policy and terminal mapping.

fanout.source: bounded static list, typed artifact collection or approved query snapshot
fanout.child_identity: hash(parent instance, fanout node, item key, definition digest); item keys unique
fanout.limits: maxItems, maxParallel, rate/spend/token quotas, per-child and aggregate deadline
fanout.isolation: separate attempt/lease/workspace/output namespace; shared write targets require serialization or declared merge protocol
fanout.dynamic_expansion: children may propose further items but controller admits them against depth/count/budget caps

join.policy: all | allSettled | quorum(k or percentage) | race | reduce
join.success/failure_thresholds: typed, predeclared, risk-aware; quorum cannot waive mandatory child/gate
join.ordering: aggregate by declared stable item key or child ordinal, never completion order
join.duplicates/missing: deduplicate child IDs; missing/timed-out status represented explicitly
join.race: winner selected by first controller-committed qualifying event; other children cancelled/cleaned; late outputs quarantined
join.merge: deterministic reducer version+digest; semantic/code conflict becomes gate, not last writer wins

composition: Subfactory reference is immutable {registry, name, version/digest, entrypoint}; alias resolves once at parent admission.
Parent passes a capability subset, budget slice, typed inputs, trace/correlation and cancellation scope. Child cannot escalate permissions.
Child exposes typed outcomes/events only through its interface; internal roles/state are private. Parent stores child instance and definition digest.
No recursive cycle unless explicitly tail-recursive with maxDepth and proven decreasing budget. Static compiler rejects graph/subfactory cycles otherwise.

Composition lock records transitive digests, schemas, tool/plugin versions and compatibility constraints. Maximum nesting is policy bounded; GitHub’s reusable-workflow depth/permission reduction is precedent, not the portable limit [S17].
Cancellation propagates parent-to-child. Child failure maps through declared outcome mapping. Compensation/cleanup order is reverse topological across effect dependencies.
scheduling: Ready-set scheduling is deterministic from priority class, age, deadline, dependency and tenant fairness; LLM ranking may be an advisory feature only.
Use queues and fenced leases. Do not confuse GitHub Actions concurrency groups with an atomic work lease.
Reserve aggregate budgets before fanout. Release unused reservation only after receipt/reconciliation.
orchestration_and_composition.sources_note: Parallel platforms disagree on fail-fast, race and output ordering; the DSL must declare these rather than inherit engine defaults [S12-S17][S31-S35].

deterministic_precedence: CONTINUE only when all guards prove eligible
continue_only_if: no unresolved blocking question or contradictory authoritative decision
risk class and affected scope inside approved autonomy profile
capability lease is least privilege and current
required deterministic gates pass on exact hashes
remaining reserved budget covers work plus cleanup
action is reversible/idempotent or separately approved
confidence/novelty policy is satisfied; model confidence is never sole evidence
clarification_triggers: two or more materially different interpretations change observable acceptance
acceptance oracle is absent, circular, authored only by candidate, or conflicts with intent
source evidence conflicts above a configured materiality threshold
decision owner or approver cannot be resolved deterministically
requested action exceeds declared interface or output schema
approval_triggers: new/changed product decision or READY spec
R2+ behavior change/merge/release per repository policy
exception, waiver, ambiguity acceptance, irreversible/destructive action, novel incident remediation
join conflict or partial result that changes committed scope
escalation_triggers: security signal, suspected prompt injection/exfiltration or unauthorized effect
unknown external effect, stale/fenced worker mutation, repeated deterministic failure
budget >=80% with no bounded completion plan; hard cap at 100%
deadline/SLO breach, human timeout, approver conflict/unavailable quorum
uncertainty score above policy threshold or evidence disagreement unresolved after one bounded research pass
stop_triggers: kill switch, legal hold or cancellation
candidate attempts to access/modify hidden evals, policy, permissions, audit or promotion authority
irreversible effect lacks exact authorized approval and tested recovery
human_need_policy.probabilistic_signals: Novelty, semantic uncertainty, disagreement and anomaly scores may only raise risk/request review. Thresholds are versioned per task class and calibrated on local labeled outcomes with abstention. They cannot grant access, lower risk, waive gates or approve.
human_need_policy.decision_timeout: Every human request declares deadline, reminders, escalation target and fail-closed result (deny, defer, pause or cancel). Never default-approve.

automation_classes.SAFE_NOW: read-only normalization/search; bounded planning draft; deterministic validation; isolated candidate artifact; known idempotent runbook; predeclared canary abort/rollback
automation_classes.CONDITIONAL: locally proven R0/R1 branch/PR work and sampled low-risk promotion within allowlist
automation_classes.HUMAN_GATE: intent/readiness, R2+, privilege, protected controls, production/high-risk actions
automation_classes.UNSUPPORTED: autonomous roadmap/value tradeoff, silent ambiguity, self-approval, grader/policy/permission self-edit, novel high-impact remediation, irreversible operations, unattended end-to-end ownership

human_need_policy.evidence: MCP only says humans SHOULD be able to deny tools, so the runtime must convert consequential classes to enforced MUST-level policy [S24]. OWASP excessive-agency and prompt-injection guidance plus AgentDojo justify default deny and authority outside the model [S25][S30].

factory_as_code_schema.design: YAML is authoring syntax; JSON Schema validates structure; a compiler resolves imports and emits a normalized immutable graph/lock digest. A policy engine evaluates authorization. Runtime state/events use separately versioned schemas. This separation follows JSON Schema dialect practice and OWS separation of DSL versus document version [S07][S31].
versioning: apiVersion controls language semantics; metadata.version is semantic definition version; digest identifies exact transitive compiled content.

Patch: corrections with identical semantics; minor: additive optional behavior/migrations; major: incompatible artifacts/states/authority. Runtime compatibility is an explicit constraint, not inferred.
Aliases/channels are mutable pointers. Resolve once and pin digest on admission. In-flight instances never take “latest.”
Unknown fields fail closed except namespaced x-* annotations. Unknown required event/artifact versions quarantine.
Definition activation uses validate -> deterministic plan/diff -> owner approval -> atomic activate; last valid stays active on failure, matching Warp’s safe apply precedent [S01].
Schema migration cannot mutate history. Use adapters/upcasters for reads or an explicit signed checkpoint migration with rollback; retain old workers/definitions until drain.
factory_as_code_schema.concrete_example_yaml:
apiVersion: factory.agent-os.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Factory
metadata:
  name: issue-to-verified-change
  version: 1.4.0
  compatibility: {requiresRuntime: ">=0.6 <1.0"}
spec:
  immutableRunSnapshot: true
  imports:
    - {name: research, ref: registry.example/research@sha256:abc..., interface: research/v1}
  policyRefs:
    - {ref: git+https://example/policy.git//factory.rego?ref=<full-sha>, digest: sha256:def...}
  artifactTypes:
    Spec: {schema: schemas/spec-2.1.json, compatibility: backward}
    Decision: {schema: schemas/decision-1.0.json, retention: project}
    Patch: {schema: schemas/patch-1.0.json, provenance: required}
    Evidence: {schema: schemas/evidence-1.2.json, provenance: required}
  roles:
    foreman:
      kind: advisory-router
      identity: factory-router
      instructions: {ref: prompts/foreman.md, digest: sha256:...}
      tools: [repo.read, issue.comment.propose]
      input: [Spec]
      output: [RouteProposal, Question]
      authority: {stateTransitions: false, approve: false, escalateCapability: false}
    implementer:
      kind: worker
      isolation: ephemeral
      tools: [repo.read, branch.write, test.run]
      capabilityProfile: low-risk-branch
      output: [Patch, Evidence]
    verifier:
      kind: verifier
      separation: {differentPrincipal: true, cleanWorkspace: true}
      tools: [repo.read, test.run]
      output: [Verification]
  budgets:
    default:
      wall: PT45M
      tokens: 200000
      cost: {currency: USD, amount: "20.00"}
      toolCalls: 300
      attempts: 2
      fanout: 8
      depth: 3
      diffLines: 800
      reserveForCleanup: {percent: 10}
      onExhausted: escalate
  retryPolicies:
    transient:
      match: [NetworkTimeout, RateLimited, WorkerLost]
      exclude: [PolicyDenied, InvalidInput, UnknownSideEffect]
      maxAttempts: 3
      backoff: {kind: exponential, initial: PT2S, factor: 2, max: PT1M, jitter: full}
  phases:
    plan:
      entry: validate-spec
      tasks:
        validate-spec:
          kind: deterministic
          uses: builtin/schema-validate@sha256:...
          in: {spec: "$artifacts.spec"}
          out: {validated: Spec}
          then: ready-gate
        ready-gate:
          kind: gate
          checks: [noOpenQuestions, acceptanceOraclePresent]
          approval: {role: product-owner, quorum: 1, bind: [spec,factory,policy], expires: P7D}
          then: implement
    build:
      entry: implement
      tasks:
        implement:
          kind: agent
          role: implementer
          checkpoint: {on: [toolEffect, PT5M], retain: P30D}
          lease: {ttl: PT5M, heartbeat: PT1M, fencing: required}
          retry: transient
          then: verify-fanout
        verify-fanout:
          kind: fanout
          items: [unit, integration, security]
          maxParallel: 3
          child: {task: verify-one, key: "$item"}
          join: {policy: allSettled, orderBy: key, success: "all(required).passed"}
          onFailure: human-review
        verify-one:
          kind: agent
          role: verifier
          out: {result: Verification}
          then: end
        human-review:
          kind: human
          questionSchema: schemas/review-decision-1.0.json
          timeout: {after: P3D, then: deferred}
          bind: [spec,patch,evidence,factory,policy]
          then: complete
        complete: {kind: end, outcome: succeeded}
        deferred: {kind: end, outcome: deferred}
  transitions:
    - {from: plan.ready-gate, event: gate.passed, to: build.implement}
    - {from: build.implement, event: task.succeeded, to: build.verify-fanout}
  events:
    ingress: {format: CloudEvents/1.0, dedupeBy: id, schemas: schemas/events/}
  failure:
    unknownEffect: reconcile
    security: {transition: escalated, revokeAllLeases: true}
  cleanup:
    always:
      - {uses: builtin/revoke-leases@sha256:..., idempotent: true}
      - {uses: builtin/delete-workspace@sha256:..., retry: transient}
    compensationOrder: reverseTopological
    failureOutcome: cleanup_failed
  observability:
    traceContext: W3C
    audit: {appendOnly: true, hashChain: true}
  evolution:
    aliases: {stable: "1.4.0"}
    inFlight: pin
    migration: explicit
  acceptance:
    success: "phases.allRequiredSucceeded && gates.allPassed && cleanup.requiredSatisfied"
factory_as_code_schema.warp_delta: Warp v1alpha1 should be treated as one adapter/import format. Its schema describes configuration, not live orchestration. Compile its agents/automations/runners/scorers into role/trigger/resource/eval records, but require explicit phase/transition/artifact/budget/gate/retry/cleanup/composition extensions before claiming a general factory DSL [S01][S02].

factory_definition_release: Author branch -> schema/reference/type/cycle/capability/lint validation -> compile transitive lock/digest -> graph/model/security/replay tests -> plan diff including authority increases -> required CODEOWNERS/policy approvals -> sign -> atomic activate alias -> shadow selected triggers -> canary admissions -> promote or alias rollback. Existing runs stay pinned.
durable_user_decision: Persist request -> normalize candidates without losing raw digest -> resolve decision owner -> research/options if bounded -> open typed Question -> WAITING_HUMAN checkpoint -> authenticate answer -> show material normalized consequence -> commit Decision revision -> invalidate dependent spec/approval/tasks -> recompile affected plan -> resume. Timeout follows declared deny/defer/escalate.
parallel_build: Admit exact READY spec -> reserve total/cleanup budgets -> issue fenced implementation lease -> checkpoint before/after effects -> publish patch/evidence -> fan out immutable exact-head verification -> allSettled join in stable key order -> deterministic required-check gate -> independent review on exact hashes -> handoff/merge authority -> reconcile receipts -> reverse-topological cleanup.
research_subfactory: Compile question/items/fields/time range/evidence policy -> bounded fanout per item/source route -> primary-source artifact capture with provenance -> schema validate each result -> join allSettled -> conflict/dedup audit -> durable user decisions for scope/conflicts -> report artifact -> scheduled evidence refresh creates a new evidence/report revision, never overwrites claims.
failure_and_resume: Worker loss -> expire/fence lease -> inspect last checkpoint/effect receipts -> if effect unknown, RECONCILING -> transient retry with new attempt/epoch if budget -> deterministic failure replan/escalate -> on cancellation stop fanout, compensate declared reversible effects, revoke credentials, clean resources -> terminal only after cleanup invariant.
composition: Parent pins subfactory interface+digest -> validates typed input/capability/budget subset -> creates child with correlation/cancellation scope -> consumes only declared outcome artifacts -> explicit join/failure mapping -> parent cleanup owns leaked-child sweep.
end_to_end_workflows.source_basis: The flow combines Warp’s role/human-handoff model [S03] with durable runtime patterns [S08-S19], rather than leaving routing and gates only in foreman prose.

maximum_safe_loop: Observe correlated outcomes with exact factory/model/tool/policy/artifact versions.
Triage and deduplicate; redact/privacy review; human-curate material failures and labels.
Create immutable eval case/dataset revision with provenance, holdout/adversarial slices and protected expected results.

Candidate agent proposes the smallest prompt/router/tool/workflow/code change as a PR. It has no write or discovery access to hidden cases, graders, thresholds, policy, permissions, audit or promotion credentials.
Run schema/security/replay/model tests and repeated stochastic offline comparisons against the current version; report per-risk slices, cost/latency, uncertainty and regressions.

Independent protected evaluator identity runs hidden tests and calibrates model graders against blinded qualified humans. Any protected invariant regression rejects regardless of composite score [S28].
Shadow on live inputs with zero authority, then canary only inside a preapproved low-risk capability cohort with exposure/error/spend/deadline limits and automatic kill/rollback.

Independent promotion authority approves the exact candidate/eval/policy digests. Activate atomically, retain prior version and monitor delayed outcomes/drift; rollback automatically on predeclared signals.
protected_outside_candidate: canary exposure/stop rules and rollback target
self_improvement_boundary.warp_comparison: Warp correctly keeps self-improvement at PR proposal and review, but published docs use LLM scorer classifications and do not document candidate isolation from graders/held-out sets or an automated shadow/canary rollback promotion protocol [S04][S05]. Therefore it is evidence for proposal workflow, not for autonomous safe promotion.
cannot_safely_be_autonomous: choosing product goals/roadmap or resolving value conflicts
consent, privacy/legal interpretation and security exceptions
authorizing new privileges, production roles or destructive/irreversible effects
candidate changing its own protected tests, grader, threshold, policy, permissions, audit or promotion authority
semantic acceptance where no independent oracle exists
novel high-impact incident command or rollback failure response
self_improvement_boundary.reason: Reward/grader hacking is documented, prompt injection remains unsolved, and multi-agent systems show coordination/verification failures [S28][S29][S30]. “Fully self-improving” is therefore bounded to automatic propose/evaluate/shadow/canary/rollback under externally owned controls.

static_schema: Validate authoring documents against pinned JSON Schema dialect; reject duplicate IDs, unresolved refs, illegal override/unknown required keys, invalid durations/currency and capability broadening.
Resolve and hash every import/tool/prompt/model/image/policy/schema. Verify signatures/allowlists and generate an SBOM/composition lock.

Compile graph; prove one entry, explicit terminal paths, reachability, no unintended cycles, valid scoping, compatible artifact edges, finite recursion/fanout, a gate before each sensitive effect, and cleanup from every exit.
semantic_and_model_tests: Exhaustively enumerate finite state/event pairs; assert invalid transitions fail closed and terminal/approval/lease/budget invariants always hold.
Property-based generated graphs/events; deterministic replay equality; event upcaster and checkpoint migration compatibility corpus.
Model-check concurrent claims, lease expiry/reclaim, cancellation races, join quorum/race, approval invalidation, budget reservation and compensation order.
Golden cross-runtime conformance suite for success/failure/retry/catch/join/cancel/timeout semantics; engines may advertise only passed capabilities.
fault_tests: Crash before/after event commit, outbox dispatch, external effect and receipt; duplicate/reorder/drop callbacks; clock skew; partition; throttling; poisoned event; worker loss; artifact-store outage; cleanup failure.
Verify no blind replay, no stale worker attachment, bounded retry, correct UNKNOWN_EFFECT reconciliation and eventual lease/token revocation.
security_tests: Prompt/tool/indirect injection, malicious repository/dependency/MCP/A2A data, confused deputy, schema smuggling, path/shell injection, secret exfiltration, SSRF, cache/artifact poisoning.
Prove candidate cannot read/write protected graders/policy/audit/promotion; test tenant/role/path/egress isolation and capability non-escalation.
Sign/verify artifacts and plans; tamper, replay and downgrade tests; sensitive trace redaction because SDK tracing can retain data [S23].
evaluation: Fixed deterministic acceptance + fresh/private temporal holdouts + adversarial/metamorphic cases + repeated stochastic trials.
Predeclare primary metric, risk slices, equivalence/noninferiority margins, confidence intervals, cost/latency/reviewer effort and stop rules.
Measure full funnel: admitted -> correct durable outcome -> retained/no incident, not PR count or judge score. Calibrate graders to blinded experts and record disagreements [S28].
acceptance_gates: 0 unexplained unauthorized effects/stale commits in fault tests
rollback and credential-revocation drills pass within declared objectives
no schema activation can partially apply; last known-good remains
local canary meets predeclared quality/safety/cost criteria; otherwise rollback
validation_strategy.validation_limit: Tests prove encoded properties, not complete intent or future adversarial safety. Human/product and specialist judgments remain where the oracle is incomplete.

implementation_recommendation.core_decision: Build a small deterministic control plane and compiler around immutable typed artifacts, event-sourced state, transactional outbox, fenced leases and external policy. Treat Warp/agent frameworks as adapters/workers, not the authority.
stage_0_spec_2_weeks: Freeze v1alpha1 authoring/event/artifact schemas and state catalog.
Create compiler/normalized IR, composition lock and conformance fixtures.
Define role/capability/risk policy, exact-hash approval and cleanup invariants.
Import Warp v1alpha1 read-only and report unsupported general-DSL constructs.
stage_1_shadow_3_5_weeks: PostgreSQL aggregate/event/outbox tables plus object store; schema registry and OPA/Cedar-style policy adapter.
Read-only triggers, deterministic scheduler, decision/question ledger, checkpoint/replay and desired/observed reconciler.
No agents receive write tools. Inject crash/duplicate/reorder/lease faults for at least 14 days.
stage_2_bounded_execution_4_8_weeks: One repository, one low-risk factory, ephemeral worker and short-lived branch-only capability.
Typed patch/evidence artifacts, exact-head independent verification, human merge, always cleanup.
Hard wall/token/cost/tool/retry/diff/fanout limits and kill switch.
stage_3_parallel_composition: Add bounded fanout/allSettled deterministic joins and one pinned research subfactory after single-worker invariants hold.
Avoid shared concurrent writes; use proposal branches and deterministic/human conflict merge.
Publish runtime capability/conformance matrix, not a portability claim.
stage_4_governed_improvement: Protected evaluator service/dataset namespace; candidate PR only.
Offline -> shadow -> narrow canary -> signed promotion -> automatic rollback; human owns graders, policy, permissions and promotion.
technology_profile: PostgreSQL transaction/outbox for MVP; object store by digest; JSON Schema 2020-12; CloudEvents envelope; W3C Trace Context; OPA/Cedar-like external policy; Sigstore/in-toto/SLSA provenance.

Use Temporal only when long waits/history/replay/operational volume justify its code/replay complexity. Use Argo/GitHub Actions for bounded compute/CI adapters, not as the canonical long-lived state store.
implementation_recommendation.build_vs_buy: Warp provides the closest managed UX and useful v1alpha1 resources, but its Early Access schema omits the required general orchestration contract. Adopt it as a front-end/worker integration only if export, identity, policy, audit and deterministic state requirements are verified in a pilot.
implementation_recommendation.go_no_go: Do not enable autonomous merge/deploy or candidate promotion until local representative denominators, protected invariant results, review cost, reverts/escapes, fault drills and rollback objectives meet predeclared thresholds.

conflicts.conflict: Warp calls the factory self-improving, but also says nothing is adopted automatically.
conflicts.resolution: Use “self-improving” only for automated failure aggregation and PR proposal [S04]. The requested maximum adds evaluation/shadow/canary/rollback automation while keeping protected controls and promotion external; it does not claim recursive autonomous authority.

conflicts.conflict: Warp documentation says definition files are source of truth, while work items/runs/metrics are never written there [S01].
conflicts.resolution: Git is authoritative only for desired immutable factory versions. The transactional runtime/event store is authoritative for executions; integrations are projections.

conflicts.conflict: Warp’s foreman dynamically skips/routes stages, whereas a safe runtime requires explicit statically checked transitions [S03].
conflicts.resolution: Allow the model to emit a typed RouteProposal among compiler-declared edges. The deterministic controller checks policy/guards and commits.

conflicts.conflict: Workflow platforms differ on retries, cleanup, branch failure, ordering and delivery: ASL/Argo/GitHub/Temporal defaults are not interchangeable [S09][S12-S17][S35][S42].
conflicts.resolution: Make every semantic dimension explicit in normalized IR and publish a per-runtime conformance matrix. Reject deployment when an adapter cannot implement required semantics.

conflicts.conflict: ASL Standard uses “exactly-once” state execution language, while queues/callbacks and external systems remain duplicable [S42].
conflicts.resolution: Never claim end-to-end exactly once. Use at-least-once handling, idempotency keys, outbox receipts and reconciliation for effects.

conflicts.conflict: LLM scorer/evaluator feedback is convenient, but grader hacking and weak-oracle risk undermine self-promotion [S05][S28].
conflicts.resolution: Use LLM graders only as calibrated evidence. Hide/protect evaluator inputs and require deterministic invariants plus independent promotion authority.

conflicts.conflict: Agent frameworks promote dynamic handoffs, while independent MAST evidence identifies coordination and verification failure modes [S22][S29].
conflicts.resolution: Default to single-worker deterministic pipelines. Add fanout only for independent shards with typed joins/objective verification.

conflicts.conflict: MCP says a human SHOULD be able to deny tool invocations [S24], but consequential factory controls need fail-closed enforcement.
conflicts.resolution: Host policy upgrades sensitive actions to MUST require exact approval/deny; never rely on protocol UI guidance.

uncertainties.unknown: Warp’s hosted runtime implementation, isolation, exact work-item state model, retry/dedup/lease/checkpoint/reconciliation semantics and production outcome denominators are not public.
uncertainties.impact: Cannot adopt Warp as canonical authority without contractual/pilot verification.
uncertainties.mitigation: Request schema/runtime/export/security documentation; instrument a shadow pilot and fault-test callbacks.

uncertainties.unknown: No validated universal translation exists across Temporal, Argo, ASL, GitHub Actions and Warp because cancellation, join, retry and history semantics differ.
uncertainties.mitigation: Target a normative IR and capability profiles; conformance-test each adapter and fail compile on semantic gaps.

uncertainties.unknown: Best fanout, nesting and budget limits depend on workload distributions, rate limits and correlated agent errors.
uncertainties.impact: Static defaults could waste cost or amplify failures.
uncertainties.mitigation: Start single-worker; measure local full-funnel outcomes; bound and tune per task class.

uncertainties.unknown: No universal calibrated uncertainty/confidence threshold safely decides when semantic human input is needed.
uncertainties.impact: Over-asking creates delay; under-asking creates silent intent errors.
uncertainties.mitigation: Deterministic triggers dominate; probabilistic scores only raise risk and are calibrated locally with abstention.

uncertainties.unknown: Public evidence does not quantify long-horizon retained benefit or rare-harm rate for automatically canaried factory changes.
uncertainties.impact: Promotion thresholds cannot be borrowed from vendors or benchmarks.
uncertainties.mitigation: Pre-register local metrics, human-calibrated holdouts, small cohorts, error budgets and automatic rollback.

uncertainties.unknown: Some official documentation is rolling and may have changed between product releases; future-dated cutoff behavior cannot be independently reproduced here beyond accessible documents and version tags.
uncertainties.mitigation: Archive/digest sources and schemas at implementation/procurement time; pin runtime versions.

confidence.overall: High (0.89) for the proposed safety/state/artifact architecture and for documented open workflow primitives; medium (0.72) for current Early Access Warp capability boundaries; low (0.35) for claims of portability or unattended end-to-end/self-promoting reliability.

claim_level.Warp v1alpha1 files/schema and human-rev: high — direct docs and live generated schema [S01-S05].
claim_level.need for protected authority and conserv: medium-high — security guidance plus independent benchmark/trace research [S25][S29][S30][S39].
claim_level.recommended DSL/runtime correctness: medium-high as an implementable synthesis; it still requires conformance, fault and local outcome validation.

confidence.method_note: Claims from vendor docs establish availability/contract, not effectiveness. Independent studies are used to challenge safety and multi-agent assumptions; no numerical estimates were averaged across incompatible tasks.
